framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 1, Build and Validate item 2, p. 14
requirement_paraphrase: Champion-model selection should include fairness metric assessment, with metrics within a threshold defined earlier for sensitive features; failures should be justified.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Compare results with pre-defined thresholds then review failure cases; adjust thresholds only with documented evidence; break results down by sub-category and attack technique, quantify variance and confidence intervals across runs, and analyse failures qualitatively including faults in the LLM judge.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Define the use cases and contexts where structured human feedback such as GAI red-teaming is most beneficial; engage in internal and external evaluations, red-teaming and impact assessments with representative AI actors; verify those conducting structured human feedback exercises are not directly involved in developing the same model.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
requirement_paraphrase: AISI states it tests leading AI systems before they are released and collaborates with AI companies, with pre-deployment access to leading models; it open-sources evaluation tools such as Inspect.

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (3 April 2025) - federal agency use of AI [added beyond assigned scope]
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct ongoing testing and periodic human review of high-impact AI, where feasible, to identify adverse impacts on performance and security, including privacy, civil rights and civil liberties violations; monitoring must detect changes after deployment and in context of use.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends systematic cybersecurity code review, testing and formal approval of all AI-generated code before use in development, integration or production.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience to abuse for attacking other systems, generative-AI attacks such as prompt injection, and ML attacks such as adversarial examples, data poisoning, membership inference, model extraction; verify fine-tuning does not compromise safety and security controls.

framework: China - Provisions on Deep Synthesis (in force 10 Jan 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Security assessment is also required before launching new products or functions with public opinion properties or social mobilisation capacity.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Processes for independent review can improve effectiveness of testing and mitigate internal bias and conflicts of interest.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Data scientists are to test AI systems to assess risks, confirm intended performance and compliance with healthcare and safety regulations, assess robustness, fairness and accuracy, and document metrics and logs; data users identify groups at risk of disparate outcomes and report use of relevant attributes.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical specification explaining how to apply the ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 testing series to AI systems using a risk-based approach to select testing practices and techniques; published Nov 2025, 34 pages.

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
clause_or_page: Ch. 10.2 (Quality Assurance Process), approx. pp.85-87 (verify against print)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes Dubai Digital Authority applying QA protocols to all its AI systems: end-to-end testing cycles, performance benchmarking, user acceptance testing and continuous quality audits, with criteria customised per quadrant.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: Hold a systematic pre-production review presenting performance, explainability and fairness metrics to decision makers; set a frequency (time- or event-based) and process for re-testing deployed systems; keep a strategy for independent oversight of development and deployment.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and test datasets must reflect the target population's diversity; regular data representativeness audits must be done at defined checkpoints with subgroup gaps flagged; bias detection techniques must be implemented and mitigation traceable.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers are required (per MDS-REQ 1) to show no unacceptable risk and that benefits outweigh residual risk; safety requirements should include evaluation results on algorithm limitations and performance; a risk management review per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 9 should be performed before commercial release.

framework: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 (company commitments published by UK DSIT on GOV.UK; page updated 7 February 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Set thresholds at which severe risks are intolerable, assess whether thresholds have been breached, articulate mitigations, and follow explicit processes if thresholds are met, in the extreme not developing or deploying a model if mitigations cannot keep risk below thresholds.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Practical recommendations > Applies to generative AI
requirement_paraphrase: Treat LLM-generated code as inherently insecure and never use it in production without a code review; train users not to trust or rely solely on generative AI outputs; filter malicious URLs if links are included in LLM responses.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systems must resist attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter use, outputs or performance; AI-specific vulnerabilities addressed where appropriate include data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples/model evasion, confidentiality attacks and model flaws.

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: For advanced AI systems, developers are to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, including before deployment.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Design the evaluation protocol, write evaluation code, run and track results, and debug the evaluation; common bugs include degraded serving; evaluation cheating and evaluation awareness are listed as bugs tagged [Emerging Practice].

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Annexure C (AI Ethics Checklist), approx. pp. 41-46; layout scrambled in extraction, low confidence
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a lifecycle checklist (Plan and Design, Prepare Input Data, Build and Validate, Deploy and Monitor) with a column marking whether each item is binding for third parties.

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluation should be repeated rather than one-off, with timing and scope set by phase; methods may be technical (tools, red teaming) or managerial (document and policy review).

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing to identify and mitigate systemic risks.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 7, Build and Validate item 4, p. 27
requirement_paraphrase: Stakeholders and owners should review and sign off the model only after successful testing, validation and user acceptance testing rounds, before productionisation.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations Reg 10 / Commissioner materials Accreditation and Certification Framework
requirement_paraphrase: ACB checks a governance document covering fairness, transparency, accountability, security and ethics; a risk-based choice of High Risk Processing over alternatives (catalogued risks, necessity, proportionality, mitigations); and transparency to data subjects. Evidence examples: policies, AI DPIAs, risk registers, privacy notices.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 4.1 / Process 4.1.1, p.29 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Carry out regular safety and harm tests (e.g. hallucination, toxicity) using use-case-appropriate benchmarks and red-teaming, document instructions to red-teamers, test in secure environments at several lifecycle checkpoints and before deployment, have stakeholders decide whether scores are acceptable, and share results.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: AI operators should define a suitable fallback plan and test it, including thresholds for acceptable results.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Policy on Use of AI in the Healthcare Sector (Policy/AI/0.9, 30 Apr 2018)
requirement_paraphrase: AI used in healthcare activities should have graceful-degradation mechanisms with automatic alerts; should be subject to audits and examination by the technology provider; and healthcare end-users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality and report to DoH as needed.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
clause_or_page: AI Safety Institute approach to evaluations (published 2024-02-09), sections 'AISI's approach to evaluations'
requirement_paraphrase: AISI conducts pre-deployment and post-deployment evaluations of advanced AI systems using automated capability assessments, expert red-teaming, human uplift studies and AI agent evaluations, focusing on misuse (chemical/biological, cyber), societal impacts, autonomous systems and safeguards.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Entities must run internal audits and assessments to verify compliance and report compliance status to DoH; DoH will conduct periodic audits and technical assessments of regulated entities.

framework: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Controllers and processors must test and evaluate the effectiveness of the security measures they apply to personal data.

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators of products using high-impact AI should endeavor to assess impacts on fundamental rights beforehand; public agencies should prefer products that completed such assessment.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Governance > AI quality assurance (Validation of AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Any update to an AI system must go through a quantitative testing and validation process as part of change control; teams must make sure the products, services and standards they rely on comply with the required standards set by standards development organisations (SDOs) such as ISO.

framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Suggested actions include stress-testing under likely scenarios and beyond known limits, testing under conditions similar to past incidents, chaos-engineering approaches, and documenting the range of conditions under which the system fails safely.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical report on properties, risks, methods and processes for AI in safety functions, non-AI safety functions protecting AI-controlled equipment, and AI used to develop safety functions; published Jan 2024, 73 pages.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Create measurement error models for pre-deployment metrics to show construct validity; measure or estimate and document biases or statistical variance in metrics or human feedback processes.

framework: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Before processing that uses modern technologies and poses a high risk to privacy and confidentiality, the controller must assess the impact of the planned processing. Mandatory cases include systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects by automated processing (including profiling) with legal or serious effects, and large-scale processing of sensitive data. Minimum content: description and purpose, necessity and suitability, privacy risk assessment, and mitigation measures.

framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Suggested actions include testing and evaluating systems in non-optimised conditions, measuring systems before deployment in conditions similar to expected scenarios, measuring validity (false positive/negative rates) and efficiency against ground truth in deployment context, and documenting differences between measurement setting and deployment environment.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluate fairness and bias as identified in MAP and document results.

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators of AI systems whose cumulative training compute meets a threshold set by Presidential Decree must identify, assess and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, maintain an incident monitoring and response system, and submit results to the Minister.

framework: Federal Decree-Law 45/2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Before processing that uses modern technologies and carries high privacy risk (the Article also names large-scale processing of sensitive data as a trigger), the controller must assess the impact on personal data protection; this includes systematic automated evaluation or profiling with legal or serious effects. The assessment must describe the processing, assess necessity and proportionality, identify risks and propose mitigations.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
clause_or_page: Appendix A.1.5 Structured Public Feedback, p.49-51
requirement_paraphrase: Describes participatory engagement, field testing and AI red-teaming as structured feedback methods; red-team quality depends on team expertise; diverse, interdisciplinary red teams with domain expertise are suggested; types are general public, expert, combination, and human/AI.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level, track and report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure adequate cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Deployers must use systems per instructions, assign oversight to competent trained persons, ensure input data relevance and representativeness where they control it, monitor operation, and suspend use and inform provider and authorities where a risk or serious incident arises.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: A risk assessment must be done for all AI systems and related assets; risks are tracked in a register with assigned owners.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends periodic testing of backup, recovery and rollback procedures for AI systems.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends testing AI systems by methods such as red teaming and adversarial evaluation, and validating human override.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Fully test the product before deployment, have robust assurance and regular checks of the live tool, and provide ways for users to report issues that prompt human review.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must periodically review, assess and verify algorithm mechanisms, models, data and outcomes.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A provider that concludes an Annex III system is not high-risk (e.g. narrow procedural task) must document that assessment before placing it on the market, register it under Art. 49(2) and give it to authorities on request; profiling systems always stay high-risk.

framework: UK Frontier AI Safety Commitments (AI Seoul Summit 2024)
clause_or_page: Preamble paragraph on best practices; Commitments VII-VIII
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories affirm internal and external red-teaming for severe and novel threats, publication of capabilities and limits, and public transparency on safety framework implementation, explaining how external actors are involved in assessing risk and adherence.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Analytical validation should use a large independent reference dataset reflecting the intended purpose and population (prevalence, multi-centre sourcing, demographics, justified size, not publicly available), each requirement applying unless there is sufficient evidence that it need not be met; performance should be shown to generalise through multisite investigation and subgroup analysis, and be tested against a gold standard.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must implement entity responsibility for algorithm security, including algorithm mechanism review and technology ethics review.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Overview, PDF p.2 (printed p.2); mapping, date and audiences from https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/tools/ai-verify-testing-framework/
requirement_paraphrase: Process-check framework to assess AI systems against 11 principles (transparency, explainability, reproducibility, safety, security, robustness, fairness, data governance, accountability, human agency and oversight, inclusive growth); each item has outcome, process and evidence, answered Yes/No/N/A with elaboration; mapped to NIST AI RMF, NIST GenAI Profile, Hiroshima Process code of conduct and ISO/IEC 42001.

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Business operators and R&D institutions are to establish AI governance covering risk identification, assessment and response across design, development, provision and implementation, with monitoring and evaluation involving management.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systems must achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity consistently throughout their lifecycle, and accuracy levels and metrics must be declared in the instructions for use.

framework: UAE Cabinet agentic-AI government transformation (announced 23 Apr 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Announces a phased move of half of federal government sectors and services to agentic AI within two years, with each phase tied to performance and impact assessments; ministers and entities to be evaluated on adoption.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 5, Build and Validate item 2, p. 22
requirement_paraphrase: Technical robustness requires rigorous testing, validation and re-assessment with oversight controls built into development; system integration test sign-off should involve relevant stakeholders.

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes pilot projects in each quadrant, limited in exposure with defined objectives and success metrics, to test assumptions before scaling.

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: AI providers are to ensure proper performance under usage conditions.

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
clause_or_page: Ch. 10.3 (AI Ethics Policy) and 10.2 (Initiative Approval), printed p. 87
requirement_paraphrase: States that every AI initiative under DDA must demonstrate alignment with DDA's ethical principles and undergo rigorous validation for ethical compliance across its lifecycle, and passes a standard approval workflow including technical feasibility, business case, risk evaluation and resource sign-off.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, Version 1.5 (published 20 May 2026, updated 5 June 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Test agents for safety and security before deployment, covering overall task execution, policy compliance (including routing for human approval), tool calling (right tool, permissions, inputs, order) and robustness to errors and edge cases; test entire workflows including reasoning and tool calls, and multi-agent systems.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems informing critical decisions should be subject to appropriate external audit; publishing the results should be considered.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers need to show valid clinical association, analytical/technical validation and clinical validation; clinical validation follows analytical validation, applies to all risk classes, and is evaluated before market placement and after; example metrics include sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV.

framework: Dubai AI System Ethics Self-Assessment Tool (Digital Dubai, beta)
requirement_paraphrase: Developer or operator organisations can self-assess the ethics level of an AI system (fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability) from idea stage to operation. The guidelines are recommended, not compulsory. The page suggests not proceeding with implementation unless a certain ethics performance level is reached, and says the tool is for self-assessment only and is not audited, checked or regulated.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Before first deploying certain Annex III high-risk systems, public-law bodies, private entities providing public services, and deployers of credit-scoring/insurance systems must assess fundamental rights impact (processes, affected groups, specific risks, oversight, remedies) and notify the market surveillance authority using the AI Office template.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Litmus is described as a Singapore government service for testing LLM apps of agencies with 1,600 prompts across security, specialised advice, undesirable and political content; default threshold 95 percent safe responses, adjustable; even a single failure in high-stakes hard-gate cases requires investigation.

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Continuously assess the cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents throughout the development lifecycle.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.3, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.3 (AI Supply Chain Security), printed p.20
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and manage cyber risks in the AI/ML supply chain. Guidance: regular security assessments of vendors, developers and other third parties should be run, or independent third-party assurance reports (e.g. SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001) or recognised certifications may be relied on; contracts should cover AI cyber security requirements.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: AI developers and operators should undertake reasonable data exploration and/or testing to detect prejudicial tendencies arising from inaccurate or biased data.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
clause_or_page: s3.8.2.2 body text, p.42 (heading concerns an oversight mechanism for data)
requirement_paraphrase: Privacy impact assessments should be conducted and also cover societal and ethical considerations.

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Before releasing a generative AI system, the ministry's planners are to create input/output test scenarios based on its purpose and functions, test inputs and outputs, and confirm stable operation and expected quality. Illustrative methods: checking domain-prohibited outputs, inappropriate generation and social bias, conformity with procurement specifications, and diverse/independent internal and external testing such as red teaming.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.1.4 (Change Management and Reporting), printed p.21; 3.2.3 (Patch Management), printed p.24; parent policy statements 2.1.4 (printed p.11) and 2.2.3 (printed p.12)
requirement_paraphrase: Manual changes to AI/ML models, algorithms, training data or configurations should be documented, reviewed, approved and tested in a secure environment before deployment, with a rollback plan where possible; patches and updates should be tested in a controlled environment before production.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Data protection and privacy > Accuracy: Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Test AI outputs against existing knowledge and expertise during training and testing; be transparent that outputs are statistically informed guesses; document sources.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 2.1 / Process 2.1.1, p.14 (technical testing, traditional AI)
requirement_paraphrase: For each model, run explainability methods to help users understand drivers of the model's output.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 2, Deploy and Monitor item 3, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: The AI system should be tested to ensure the combination of available data does not reveal sensitive data or break anonymity.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluate regularly for safety risks; demonstrate that the system to be deployed is safe, residual risk does not exceed tolerance, and it can fail safely, including beyond its knowledge limits.

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Each ministry's Chief AI Officer (CAIO), with planners, shall conduct use-case risk assessments and determine the risk level (including whether likely high-risk), referring to the High-Risk AI Project Finder (Appendix 1); likely high-risk cases are reported to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; the CAIO makes the final determination.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers with public opinion or social mobilisation capacity must carry out security assessments under state rules.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Implement post-deployment monitoring plans, including capturing input from users and AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery and change management.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Define, conduct and report a statistically valid analysis procedure, ideally defined in advance, that accounts for sources of variation and uncertainty and states assumptions.

framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Content distribution platforms must check metadata for implicit labels, add notices for confirmed, declared or suspected generated content, and provide a declaration tool.

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Guidelines on testing AI-based systems: difficulty of setting acceptance criteria, the test oracle problem, black-box and white-box (neural network) approaches, and test environments; published Nov 2020, 52 pages, stage 90.60 with systematic review begun Oct 2025.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Standard describing how to use formal methods to prove robust behaviour of neural networks, including selecting, applying and managing those methods; published 1 Aug 2023, 23 pages.

framework: ADGM guidance brochure - Automated individual decision-making incl. profiling
requirement_paraphrase: For AI-supported decisions: human reviewers should have the authority and competence to overturn recommendations and be trained on AI limits; risk monitoring should track how often reviewers accept or reject AI outputs; after the system is built and trained, design-phase assumptions should be tested and confirmed.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3.3 'When deploying, continuously monitor and test', case study 'GovTech: Phased rollouts of coding assistants', pp.42-43
requirement_paraphrase: Case study: GovTech (statutory board) rolled out agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, GitHub Copilot Agent Mode from Oct 2025; Claude Code from Apr 2026) after extensive tests on failure and threat vectors such as agent manipulation, hallucination and MCP server compromise and after implementing controls; phase 1 limited to GovTech employees, no MCP access and low-risk systems; before phase 2 (other agencies, then vendors) red teaming was conducted to validate guardrails, with central logging and a sandboxed MCP governance path.

framework: ADGM Office of Data Protection - Guidance on DPR 2021 Part 4 (DPIA)
requirement_paraphrase: A DPIA is required before processing likely to create high risk, and the guidance lists as triggers use of personal data in datasets used to train or refine an AI system (in the specific exception context) and profiling or automated decision-making used to decide access to a service or benefit.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.4.4 'Testing and Validation of AI/ML Systems', printed p.36 (parent policy statement 2.4.4, printed p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: The entity should keep a framework for testing and validating AI/ML systems so accuracy, reliability and performance meet defined criteria; all AI/ML systems should be rigorously tested before deployment for functionality, security and resilience, covering varied scenarios and edge cases.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes that current pre-deployment TEVV for GAI may be inadequate, non-systematically applied or mismatched to deployment context; anecdotal tests such as standardised exams do not guarantee validity; jailbreak or prompt-engineering tests may not assess validity; laboratory and benchmark settings may not predict real-world impacts.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: AI models must be rigorously validated against established performance benchmarks before deployment.

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation must include comprehensive testing across diverse datasets and contexts to confirm accuracy, safety and efficacy.

framework: EU harmonised standards work (CEN-CENELEC JTC 21)
requirement_paraphrase: prEN 18281 (evaluation methods for accurate computer vision systems) and prEN 18282 (cybersecurity specifications for AI systems, covering poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks and model flaws) are at stage 50 and flagged harmonised.

framework: Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles in Dubai
requirement_paraphrase: Technical inspections must be conducted on autonomous vehicles; an AV must pass the technical inspection prescribed by RTA to be licensed; the Director General of RTA sets inspection types, frequency and standards by resolution.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct AI red-teaming for privacy issues such as output of training data, model extraction, membership inference, revealing confidential or personal information, and tracking user location.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (version read: v1.0, 22 Jan 2026; v1.5 not read)
clause_or_page: s.2.3.2, pp.19-20 (v1.0, unchecked); in v1.5 (20 May 2026) s.2.3.2 'Before deploying, test agents', pp.39-40
requirement_paraphrase: Test in real or realistic environments that mirror production (balancing realism against risk of real-world side effects), test repeatedly across varied datasets to observe low-probability behaviours and stability, and evaluate results at scale using different methods per workflow part; the source describes current industry solutions as LLM or agent evaluators, or human evaluation (practice described, not a recommendation).

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Three-step approach: identify relevant risks and set thresholds; test in a structured manner from outputs to components; analyse results to decide whether thresholds are met. No universal baseline applies; each organisation sets its own.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Ethics > Safety, security and robustness (H3) > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Establish performance metrics measuring accuracy of outputs; test the system in a variety of scenarios including extreme or rare events; implement red teaming and record behaviour under unexpected or anomalous scenarios.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems posing high risk to basic rights must undergo pre- and post-conformity assessments in addition to ethics adherence and statutory requirements; unacceptable-risk systems are not allowed.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Testing must be done as appropriate throughout development and in any event before placing on the market or putting into service, against pre-defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to the intended purpose.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Consolidated Version No. 2, Regulation 10 (autonomous and semi-autonomous systems)
clause_or_page: Reg. 10.3.3, limbs (a)-(d); Autonomous Systems Officer appointment is limb (d)
requirement_paraphrase: A System may not be used for High Risk Processing Activities unless the Commissioner has established audit and certification requirements for such Systems, the System meets them, it processes data only for human-defined or approved purposes, and an Autonomous Systems Officer is appointed.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: If using a black-box or third-party model, assess the vendor's claim on accuracy.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A new conformity assessment is required after a substantial modification; changes pre-determined at the initial assessment for continually learning systems and recorded in the technical documentation are not substantial modifications.

framework: China - Provisions on Deep Synthesis (in force 10 Jan 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must periodically review algorithms and carry out security assessments (self or entrusted professional body) for tools generating or editing faces/voices or content affecting national security or public interest.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systems must be as resilient as possible to errors, faults and inconsistencies, with technical redundancy or fail-safe options allowed, and continual-learning systems must address feedback loops from biased outputs.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 7.1 / Process 7.1.1, p.71 (technical testing, traditional AI)
requirement_paraphrase: System owner selects fairness metrics for sensitive features and measures disparity of error rates across groups.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Run output testing (black-box end-to-end evaluation after components and mitigations are in place, reflecting real user interaction) and component testing (e.g. retrieval step in RAG, filters, system prompt) to locate failure points and catch faults masked by correct outputs.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Ethics > Accountability and responsibility (Practical recommendations and Liability)
requirement_paraphrase: Use assurance techniques to evaluate performance; establish a human-in-the-loop process to oversee and validate outputs in high-impact or high-risk situations; reconsider use if risk is too high; nominate a senior responsible owner.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.2.2(b)(vi), Annex A printed pp.10-11
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed: where codes, certifications or policy frameworks are in development or do not exist for the type and use of a System, the notice must describe the privacy-by-design and default measures implemented to comply with Article 14(3) of the Law or other applicable legislation; in such cases the Commissioner and any advisory body it establishes may request an impact assessment or convene a review and audit body to give technical and governance recommendations.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical specification giving guidance for evaluating AI systems using an AI system quality model; published 24 Jan 2024, 20 pages, stage 90.92 (due for revision); successor ISO/IEC AWI 25058 is listed as under development (stage 20.00 (registered 2025-07-25)).

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A risk management system must be established, implemented, documented and maintained as a continuous iterative lifecycle process: identify and analyse known and foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights, estimate risks under intended use and foreseeable misuse, evaluate post-market data, adopt targeted measures.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Sustainability impact assessments must be conducted for all high-impact AI systems with transparent reporting on energy, emissions and hardware.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Risk Management Protocol (ref. as extracted DoH/Protocol/DDGO/RALRM/V1/2025, V1, published and effective Oct 2025, revision Oct 2028)
clause_or_page: s3 Recommended Protocol, Risk Evaluation and Treatment, Step 4 'Control Identification', printed p.6
requirement_paraphrase: Risk controls for AI systems are identified through review of safeguards, gap analysis and stakeholder consultation, and are tested through simulations or pilot studies before full implementation to confirm they reduce risk and support AI safety and reliability.

framework: China - TC260-PG-20268A Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide: AI Application Security Guidelines, General (v1.0-202609, TC260 Secretariat, Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: At deployment, use safety guardrails to identify and block illegal content, prevent prompt injection and runaway execution chains; where third-party protection services are used, test and evaluate their security capability and service continuity; perform security checks on hardware, software and third-party tools, fix known vulnerabilities or mitigate, and track vulnerabilities to prevent supply-chain backdoors.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: Assess risks and risk levels per use case; continuously assess, measure and monitor outcomes and risks including after deployment; identify and document TEVV considerations (experimental design, data representativeness, construct validity).

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Consolidated Version No. 2, Regulation 10 (autonomous and semi-autonomous systems)
requirement_paraphrase: Accountability principle: a System must have mechanisms for responsibility and accountability; these may include internal governance and control frameworks or regular external auditing (examples only).

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct adversarial testing at a regular cadence to map and measure GAI risks; evaluate performance in real-world scenarios; verify and document that structured public feedback results are incorporated in deployment go/no-go decisions.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must ensure the system undergoes the Art. 43 conformity assessment before market placement or service, draw up the EU declaration of conformity, affix the CE marking, and on a reasoned request demonstrate conformity to national authorities.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Ethics (introductory paragraphs after the six themes, before 'Safety, security and robustness')
requirement_paraphrase: Where possible, make specific and robust measurements to assess AI systems, for example evaluating accuracy and output quality against protected characteristics in the Equality Act 2010, choosing assessments suited to the technology and use case.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Risk Management Protocol (ref. as extracted DoH/Protocol/DDGO/RALRM/V1/2025, V1, published and effective Oct 2025, revision Oct 2028)
clause_or_page: Step 10 (10.1, 10.2) Reassessment, printed p.8; Step 11 (11.1, 11.2) Review and Consultation, printed pp.8-9; KPI table p.11
requirement_paraphrase: Risk assessment reviews shall be conducted at planned intervals and should also be carried out ad hoc when significant changes occur; regular assessments shall confirm that controls are implemented and effective, and corrective actions shall be verified. When reporting to DoH, organisations must give clear, accurate and timely documentation of risk assessments, controls, incidents and corrective actions; regular reporting may include audit findings. DoH review of high-risk AI systems may include compliance audits, and DoH reviews the risk register. KPIs include an annual AI ethical incident rate threshold below 15%.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Internal-control procedure: provider verifies the QMS meets Art. 17, examines the technical documentation against Section 2 requirements, and verifies that the design/development process and post-market monitoring are consistent with the documentation.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: AI services must be secure and resilient and comply with Secure by Design principles and the Government Cyber Security Standard; build safeguards including security testing and, for generative AI, content filtering and validation checks.

framework: DHA Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare Policy (HISHD/PP-09)
requirement_paraphrase: End users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality by an independent third party, reporting to DHA-HRS as needed.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Notified-body certificates are valid for the period stated, at most five years for Annex I systems and four years for Annex III systems, extendable at the provider's request after re-assessment; where a system no longer meets Section 2 requirements the body must, applying proportionality, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless the provider takes corrective action within the deadline set by the body.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: For Annex III points 2 to 8 (critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice/democracy) providers follow the internal-control procedure of Annex VI with no notified body.

framework: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (via ODP Guidance Part 4, v1.0, Aug 2021)
requirement_paraphrase: A DPIA is required where a controller relies on the exception to deletion/anonymisation duties for data used lawfully to train or refine an AI system without risk to data subjects' rights.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 6, Plan and Design item 3, p. 24
requirement_paraphrase: If an AI system is built by a third party, owners should ensure an AI Ethics due diligence is carried out and documentation is accessible and traceable before procurement or sign-off.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.2, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.2 (Cyber Risk Management for AI/ML), printed p.19
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and mitigate AI-specific cyber security risks systematically and continuously. Guidance: cyber risk assessments should be run at regular intervals and at key lifecycle stages such as model design, data collection, training and deployment, including risks of cloud AI services that use client data.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.2(b), Annex A printed p.13 (current 10.3.2(b) would become 10.3.2(c))
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed: no one may use, operate or offer for commercial use a System that processes personal data unless the System has been tested for safety verification, including native regulatory and security design (in addition to human-defined purposes and design compliance with Reg. 10.3.1 and Commissioner audit, governance or certification requirements).

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems should be tested before deployment and regularly while in operation; measurement should include rigorous software testing and performance assessment with measures of uncertainty, benchmark comparisons and documented reporting of results.

framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Suggested actions include red-team exercises under adversarial or stress conditions, documenting red-team results, and using separate testing teams (set up under GOVERN) so that decisions about AI systems are independent; assess independence and stature of TEVV actors.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Sandboxes give a controlled environment for development, training, testing and validation under an agreed sandbox plan; authorities give guidance and supervision to identify risks, and on request supply written proof and an exit report which market surveillance authorities and notified bodies must take positively into account.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluations must be scientifically rigorous (internal validity, external validity, reproducibility) and use state-of-the-art elicitation that minimises under-elicitation and model deception (e.g. sandbagging), matching misuse actors' elicitation capability and expected deployment context.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Guidelines (Smart Dubai v1.11, English)
requirement_paraphrase: Systems informing critical decisions should be subject to appropriate external audit, and audit results of civic interest should be considered for public release. The guideline is suspended until further notice because no external auditing mechanism has been established.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Involve internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers and/or independent assessors in regular assessments; consult domain experts, users, external AI actors and affected communities as needed per risk tolerance.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Planned specification for quality assessment of prompt-based text-to-text generative AI systems, including safety assessment with red teaming; at stage 20.00 (registered Sept 2025).

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: Traditional AI: compute accuracy and compare with and without added noise. Generative AI: benchmark against time or other models and test perturbed prompts (synonyms, typos, punctuation, adversarial perturbation) with the same metric.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.4.4 (s2.4 Operational Security), printed p.14
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must secure its AI/ML systems through comprehensive testing and validation that gives assurance of their resilience against potential threats.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3 overview p.33 and s.2.3.3 'Robust change management', p.45
requirement_paraphrase: Throughout the lifecycle implement change management and version control; define triggers that start a change review (technical e.g. model updates or tool changes; environmental; performance e.g. anomalous behaviour; regulatory) and categorise changes by risk, with lighter review for minor prompt refinements, full governance review for material changes such as model updates or autonomy adjustments, and possibly an immediate re-risk assessment for critical changes affecting high-stakes decisions.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Establish a test plan and response policy, before developing highly capable models, to periodically evaluate whether the model may misuse CBRN information or capabilities and/or offensive cyber capabilities.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Notified-body procedure: the body assesses the QMS, examines technical documentation with access to training, validation and test data sets (including remote API access), may require further evidence or tests, and performs its own tests if dissatisfied with the provider's tests.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Verify the architecture can monitor outputs and recover from errors when security anomalies are detected; verify the system handles inappropriate, malicious or illegal queries properly; regularly evaluate vulnerabilities to circumvention of safety measures.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Risk Management Protocol (ref. as extracted DoH/Protocol/DDGO/RALRM/V1/2025, V1, published and effective Oct 2025, revision Oct 2028)
clause_or_page: Decision Point DP1 (Residual Risk Rating), printed pp.6-7 (avoid rule p.6; routing to Steps 6/7/10 p.7); Step 6 'Avoid High Risk System', printed p.7
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems with very high residual risk must not be implemented. Step 6, reached for very high risk, says a system classified as high risk despite existing controls must be avoided, while DP1 routes high and medium risks to mitigation (Step 7).
